findings.title: CON-AUTH-007 AC-3 anchor accepts Java 17 and so cannot show the Java 8 run
findings.description: The test passes on 1.8 or >= 17 and reads gradle/java8-tests.gradle text; under the default Java 17 build it proves nothing about running on Java 8. The comment says the evidence is the recorded runs, so the AC citation here is a marker, not a check.
findings.suggested_fix: Either mark it as non-evidence (drop the AC citation) or assert java.specification.version == 1.8 when the java8 init script property is set.

findings.title: Inverted failure message
findings.description: SEC_FLOW_008_AC4 wraps assertTrue(usable(s[1])) in catch (AssertionError) { fail("the cookie token stayed usable") } - the message fires when the token did NOT stay usable, and the try/catch adds nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with assertTrue("the cookie token stays usable", usable(s[1])).

findings.title: typ-separation helper accepts any Exception as a refusal
findings.description: refused() treats every Exception from decode as the expected typ refusal, so an NPE or a MiniJson bug while decoding a cross-typ token would count as 'typ separation'.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch the codec's documented rejection type (JwtException / the auth rejection) and fail on others.

findings.title: IR-IAM-004 AC-6 'one lock' race test almost never runs into the race it is named for
findings.description: IR_IAM_004_AC6_oneLockAndDurableFile starts two threads on a latch, and each one calls addParent(a,b) or addParent(b,a) once on a two-group graph. The check-then-insert takes microseconds, and thread wake-up jitter after go.countDown() is usually larger than that, so the two calls nearly always run one after the other. Then the second call sees the first edge and is refused as a cycle (refused.size()==1), whether or not InMemoryGroupStore holds one lock over the check and the insert. Example: remove the synchronization from InMemoryGroupStore.addParent (check under one lock, insert under another, or no lock) and all 20 rounds would still pass on almost every run. So the AC's concurrency guarantee has no real evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the race deterministic. Add a package-private hook to InMemoryGroupStore/GroupEdges that runs between the cycle check and the insert (or override a protected step in a test subclass). Thread x parks in the hook on a latch while thread y calls addParent(b,a). Then assert that y blocks until x releases it (lock held) and that exactly one edge exists at the end. Or drop the concurrency claim from the citation and keep only the durable-file half.

findings.title: 200 ms wall-clock upper bound in the bcrypt cost-cap test fails on slow CI
findings.description: SEC_TOKEN_008_AC3 measures one verify() with System.nanoTime() and asserts millis < 200 to prove that the cost-15 key schedule was skipped. On a loaded CI agent or an Android-speed JVM, a GC pause or scheduler stall, or the first-call class loading and static S-box init of Blowfish/BcryptPasswordHasher (this is the first bcrypt call in the method), can push a cheap refused verify past 200 ms. The test then fails while the product is correct. The same method then runs a real cost-15 verify (raised.verify), which takes about 2-3 s on a desktop JVM and longer on CI, with no timeout. The skipped-work property is better proven structurally.
findings.suggested_fix: Prove 'no key schedule' with a counter seam (for example a package-private Blowfish/eksBlowfish invocation counter, or a hasher hook the test can read), or at least warm the class up with a cheap verify before timing it and raise the bound to well below the cost-15 time (for example < 1000 ms). Move the cost-15 positive verify into its own test with @Test(timeout=...).

findings.title: Started apps and Auth instances are never shut down (deferred: started TestApps / fixtures not stopped)
findings.description: Every test in WebSocketWrapperTest builds an AdminFixture, which calls app.listen(0) with auth installed, and never shuts it down. FR_FLOW_008_AC8 builds two and FR_FLOW_008_AC6 two, so 10 apps stay alive in all. Each keeps its worker pool, Auth hash-slot pool and timer, cleanup scheduler, WebSocket ticker and an open server session alive in the shared test JVM. The same pattern is in OriginsTest.check (one TestApp per call), GroupAdminStoreTest.status (one TestApp per call), AuthCoreKotlinTest, AuthFacadeKotlinTest, AuthWave11KotlinTest, CallbackMatrixKotlinTest (new tests i, j, k), AuthDocsExamplesKotlinTest (about 30 Auth/TestApp builds) and Wave9KeyOwnersTest.FR_APIKEY_006_AC6 (three Auth instances whose create() starts hash threads). Thread names are unique, so no current test collides, but threads and memory grow with the suite. This was carried from the w05/w06 reviews and is still present.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the fixtures in a list and shut them down in an @After (AdminFixture.app.shutdown(5, SECONDS), TestApp's app().shutdown, Auth stop through the app's onStop). For the Kotlin tests use a try/finally or a JUnit rule.

findings.title: A fixed 50 ms sleep is the only guard against an asynchronous wrong close
findings.description: FR_FLOW_008_AC8 asserts o.server.isOpen() after each tick, then sleeps 50 ms ('a wrong asynchronous close would have reached the channel by now') and asserts channel.isOpen(). If a regression closes the session asynchronously, for example on the ticker's executor, and that close arrives later than 50 ms on a slow CI JVM, the test passes. The negative check depends on timing and gets weaker exactly where it matters.
findings.suggested_fix: Register a close listener on the server session (ws.onClose) that counts down a latch, run the ticks, then assert !latch.await(<bounded>, ...). Or make the recheck path synchronous through a test seam and drop the sleep.

findings.title: shutdown test may never put the synchronous caller in the queue before shutdown
findings.description: shutdownFailsWaitersAndRefusesLaterRequests starts the sync caller and sleeps 100 ms, assuming the caller is blocked in the queue by then. On a slow JVM the thread may reach slots.call() only after slots.shutdown(). Its AuthUnavailableException then comes from the 'refused after shutdown' path, so the test passes without proving that shutdown wakes and fails a queued synchronous waiter. Also, the finally block only counts hold down and never calls slots.shutdown(). If started.await or an earlier assertion fails, the 1-slot pool's hash and timer threads leak.
findings.suggested_fix: Wait until the sync thread is actually parked, using the RehashQueueTest pattern: loop on sync.getState() until it is WAITING or TIMED_WAITING with a deadline, or use a queued-count accessor on HashSlots. Call slots.shutdown() in finally (it is idempotent).

findings.title: FR-APIKEY-002 AC-5 tail assertion can never fail; 'after onStop no further call' is not checked by call count
findings.description: After f.stop() the test builds a fresh W8 'none' without .apiKeys(keys), calls none.auth.cleanupRun() and asserts keys.expiredCalls is unchanged. 'none' has no reference to the test's Keys instance, so the count cannot change and assertEquals(calls, keys.expiredCalls.get()) is always true. The 'after onStop no further call' half is covered only by the cleanupScheduled() flag. A regression where onStop clears the flag but a still-running scheduled task calls deleteExpired again would pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the vacuous assertion (the assertNull(none.auth.apiKeyStore()) above it is the real check for the 'without .apiKeys' half). For the onStop half, after f.stop() trigger or await the scheduler (or take the executor through a seam and assert isTerminated()), then assert keys.expiredCalls is unchanged.

findings.title: CLAIMS 8 KB total is never accepted at its boundary; the 'eightKb' document is 16 bytes
findings.description: SEC_TOKEN_002_AC2 builds justFits (exactly 8192 bytes) but expects it to be refused for its 1 KB string. It then parses 'eightKb', which is {"s":"","t":[1]} (repeat(' ',0) and repeat('1',1)), only 16 bytes. 'many' is over 8192. No CLAIMS document of exactly 8192 bytes is ever accepted, so an off-by-one that refuses total == 8192 passes this AC test. The variable name suggests the boundary was meant to be covered.
findings.suggested_fix: Build a CLAIMS document of exactly 8192 UTF-8 bytes whose strings are each at most 1 KB (for example an array of short strings padded to length), assert that it parses, then assert that one more byte is refused with the 8192 message. Rename or remove eightKb.

findings.title: assertEquals(null, made) in the catch block cannot fail
findings.description: In FR_TOKEN_003_AC5 'made' is assigned only if hash() returns, and in that case fail() throws before the catch. Inside catch(UnsupportedOperationException), made is therefore always null, so the assertion checks a value the test itself set.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the assertion (the fail() already proves that no hash string was returned), or restructure it as assertThrows-style code.

findings.title: Assertion on the test's own exception message
findings.description: throwingRoleStorePropagates ends with assertFalse(down.getMessage().isEmpty()), where 'down' is the IllegalStateException("db down") the test created. It checks no product behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the line, or assert something about the propagated exception (already done by assertEquals(down, e)).

findings.title: IR-AUTH-004 AC-8 test ends with an assertion on a local null
findings.description: val p: AuthPrincipal? = null; assertEquals(null, p?.apiKeyId) is always true. If the intent is a compile-time probe that AuthPrincipal.apiKeyId is a nullable property, the runtime assertion adds nothing and looks like a check.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace it with a typed compile probe (val k: String? = principal.apiKeyId inside the check lambda, on the real principal) or remove it.

findings.title: Dead set and tautological assertion in the Javadoc test
findings.description: IR_IAM_002_AC5 ends with Set<String> unused = Collections.emptySet(); assertTrue(unused.isEmpty()); — dead code with an assertion that cannot fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete both lines.

findings.title: Unused map in builderRefusesMisuse
findings.description: Map<String,Object> big is created and has 'unused' put into it, but it is never read. The oversize claim set is built through the builder b. This is leftover dead code that misleads readers about what is under test.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 'big' and the put.

findings.title: Superseded duplicate tests left beside their promoted versions
findings.description: lockOrderOnEveryVerBumpAndOnTheAppIssue (215-249) repeats the five ver++ calls and the key-lock/user-lock assertions of REL_APIKEY_003_AC6_lockOrderOnTheVerBumpsAndTheThreeIssuers (1163-1198) line for line. The latter calls itself its promotion and adds the PAT and admin issuers. In the same way, appIssueBehindTheFutureKeyDeletion (895-919) overlaps REL_APIKEY_003_AC4 and REL_APIKEY_004_AC2. The duplicates double the maintenance work, and one copy can drift from the other.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the two pre-promotion tests, or fold their only extra assertion (the app-issue marker staying at 5 on a failed retry) into REL_APIKEY_004_AC2.

findings.title: Copy-pasted class-file reader and JDBC fake plumbing across test files
findings.description: classFiles(...) and matches(...) are copied verbatim in VerifyUserStoreTest (380-425) and jdbc/JdbcThrottleTest (398-443). The DataSource plumbing (getLogWriter, setLoginTimeout, unwrap and so on) and the proxy, zero and invoke helpers are written four times: jdbc/FakeJdbc, jdbc/RecordingJdbc (twice, including the Delegating base), jdbc/SqliteFixture and IamJdbcDialectTest.OneRowJdbc. A fix to one copy, for example handling a JarFile code source, will not reach the others.
findings.suggested_fix: Move classFiles/matches into one shared test helper (the testFixtures or auth test package). Have FakeJdbc, SqliteFixture and OneRowJdbc extend RecordingJdbc.Delegating and share one proxy/zero helper.

findings.title: Docs-example test writes its SQLite database to the system temp directory
findings.description: 'docs auth schema' uses java.io.File.createTempFile("auth-docs", ".db") with deleteOnExit(). The database, and any -journal or -wal file SQLite creates next to it, live in the shared /tmp until the JVM exits. A crashed or killed test run leaves them behind, and deleteOnExit never removes the side files. Every other SQLite test in the chunk uses a JUnit TemporaryFolder.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a TemporaryFolder @get:Rule (Kotlin: @get:Rule val tmp = TemporaryFolder()) and create the database under it.

findings.title: Wall-clock upper bounds used as proof that a call does not block
findings.description: fullQueueDropsWithoutBlockingAndAcceptsLater asserts that the 101st offer returns within 1 s of System.nanoTime(). The same pattern is in Wave9KeyAuthTest.SEC_APIKEY_004_AC8 (two in-memory requests < 3 s, lines 381-384) and HashSlotsTest.fullQueueRefusesImmediatelyWithoutRunningTheWork (< 1000 ms at line 83, already implied by the await(1, SECONDS) on line 82). A stalled CI JVM can break these bounds while the code is correct. In the HashSlots case the bound is redundant. The non-blocking property is better shown structurally: offer() returned false while the worker is still parked in the hasher, and nothing waited on the queue.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the structural assertions and drop the timing ones, or raise the bounds well above the blocking alternative (the blocking alternative here is 'forever', so any generous bound such as 10 s works) and remove the redundant HashSlots line.

findings.title: SEC-TOKEN-009 AC-8 Servlet half: the "answered while the failure waits" assertion cannot fail
findings.description: healthAt is taken right after the synchronous /health call returns, and failedAt is taken after failing.get(...), which is only called after /health has returned. System.nanoTime is monotonic, so failedAt >= healthAt on every run and `healthAt < failedAt` holds whatever the server does. Scenario: the floor is changed to sleep inside the request thread, or Jetty serves /health only after the delayed 401 is written; the test still passes. Nothing checks that the failing login was still pending when /health answered (Thread.sleep(10) does not even guarantee the login reached the server first). The SRS evidence for SEC-TOKEN-009 AC-8 (VE-2, Servlet half) therefore does not cover the concurrency clause of the AC.
findings.suggested_fix: After /health returns, assert !failing.isDone() (the failure is still waiting), and time each exchange from its own start as the TinyHttpd half does. Before sending /health, wait until the login has reached the server (for example a latch in a LoginThrottle.retryAfter test double, or a RecordingLogger/access-log line), not a fixed 10 ms sleep.

findings.title: TinyHttpd AC-8 check compares durations from separate starts, so it does not show the two requests overlapped
findings.description: health.millis and failed.millis are each measured from that request's own start. If the pool thread opens its socket late (the 10 ms Thread.sleep is the only ordering) and /health is answered before the failing login arrives, the failure still takes T + 1.25T, so `health.millis + 10 < failed.millis` holds although the two requests never overlapped. The AC clause "a concurrent non-auth request is answered while the failure waits" is then not shown. With 4 workers a floor that blocks its worker would also pass, but that half is covered by the AC-5 test. Earlier waves deferred this as "floor-test wall-clock margins" (W10); it is still there.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert !failing.isDone() right after /health returns. Order the requests by an event (the login reached the throttle or hash slot) rather than Thread.sleep(10).

findings.title: AC-5 check compares a loaded-server latency with one idle-server probe
findings.description: floorMillis comes from a single probe on an idle server, and health.millis is measured while 50 logins each run a 200 000-iteration PBKDF2. On a slow 2-vCPU CI or an Android-speed JVM, CPU contention can push /health past one idle floor, and the test then fails for timing alone. The sleep max(20, floor/4) is also a fixed wall-clock wait. This is the deferred W10 "floor-test wall-clock margins" item; it is still present.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep `pending > 0` as the main signal. Bound health.millis by a margin derived from the probe (for example < 0.5 * 50 * floorMillis / workers, which is what a worker-held floor would cost) rather than by one floor.

findings.title: Expected AuthRejection on refresh-token reuse has no fail() when nothing is thrown
findings.description: The second refresh(pair.refreshToken) is wrapped in try/catch(AuthRejection) with no fail() after the call. If reuse detection started returning a new pair and still fired onRefreshTokenReused, the test would pass, although the docs example (auth.md#35) says a reused token is rejected.
findings.suggested_fix: Add fail("a reused refresh token was accepted") after the second refresh, or use assertThrows.

findings.title: Two docs-example tests run with no assertion
findings.description: `docs auth csrf guarded route` (133-142) and `docs auth cors before install` (159-170) only build and install. They pass as long as nothing throws, so a guard that let a POST without a CSRF token through, or an install that dropped the CORS middleware, would not be noticed. As T11 compile checks they are acceptable, but their names suggest a behaviour check.
findings.suggested_fix: Either name them as compile checks, or send one request through an InMemoryHttpAdapter (for example POST /api/posts without the CSRF token gives 403, and the preflight carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin).

findings.title: The "lockout and websocket wrapper" test checks neither the lockout nor the wrapper
findings.description: Lockout.after(3).forMinutes(1) is set but no failed login is ever attempted. The auth.webSocket { } wrapper is registered on an app that is never started or sent an upgrade, so its lambda never runs. `auth.describe().contains("auth")` is close to always true. Only the token-service half is asserted.
findings.suggested_fix: Add assertions that exercise the lockout (three failed passwordLogin attempts lead to the lock), or drop "lockout and websocket wrapper" from the name and keep it as a compile check.

findings.title: The JDBC half of "refresh token stores from Kotlin" is a tautology
findings.description: The comment says the in-memory, file and JDBC stores share one SPI, but the JDBC store is checked only by `assertEquals("JdbcRefreshTokenStore", JdbcRefreshTokenStore::class.java.simpleName)`, which compares a class with its own name and cannot fail. Nothing calls JdbcRefreshTokenStore from Kotlin.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a JdbcRefreshTokenStore over a TemporaryFolder SQLite DataSource (as AuthWave6JdbcKotlinTest does) to the `stores` list, or remove the line.

findings.title: The SQLite database is a File.createTempFile in the system temp dir, cleaned only by deleteOnExit
findings.description: File.createTempFile("naru", ".db") plus deleteOnExit leaves the file behind when the Gradle test JVM is killed. SQLite's -journal or -wal side files are not covered by deleteOnExit at all. The sibling AuthWave6JdbcKotlinTest uses the TemporaryFolder rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a @get:Rule TemporaryFolder and put the database in tmp.newFolder().

findings.title: Jar names hard-code 0.10.0, and the module-list check matches exact whitespace
findings.description: jar() builds "<module>-0.10.0<suffix>.jar". The 0.11.0 version bump will make CON_AUTH_001_AC3 fail on a missing file, not on a placement error. CON_AUTH_001_AC2 checks for a literal including a newline and 19 spaces of indentation, so reformatting build.gradle breaks it with no change in behaviour. The same hard-coding exists in BuildLayoutTest, CentralStagingTest and PublishedPomTest.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the version from a system property set from project.version (as naruserve.rootDir is), and parse naruModules with a regex that tolerates whitespace.

findings.title: Duplicate transient-hash tests, and the AC-2 "negative control" does not test the checker
findings.description: transientHashLimitIsDocumented (38-50) and DR_IAM_001_AC7_transientHashLimitInJavadocAndDocs (78-95) assert the same KO_HASH/EN_HASH and the same AuthUser Javadoc, so a change has to be made twice. In CON_AUTH_005_AC2 the "negative control" `assertFalse(ko.contains("`NoSuchAuthType`"))` (190) only checks that the page lacks a made-up string. It never runs the missing-type logic on an absent type, so a broken check (for example publicUtilsTypes() returning the wrong names) would not be caught. Compare CON_AUTH_005_AC3, which feeds apiEntryGaps a synthetic page.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the unannotated duplicate. Make the control run the same membership check over a list with a fake type and assert that it is reported missing.

findings.title: cited() accepts any line holding the AC token within four lines above any @Test
findings.description: The Java branch matches the AC token on any line, such as an assertion message string or a comment near the end of the previous method body, and then accepts the next @Test within four lines. Scenario: the owner test of SEC-HTTP-001 AC-2 is deleted, but a neighbouring test ends with assertEquals("SEC-HTTP-001 AC-2 ...", ...) and is followed by another @Test. The gate still reports the AC as cited. It also does not check that the cited method is in a class that runs (it could be abstract or a helper).
findings.suggested_fix: Only count comment lines (`//` or `*`) that are followed by annotations or blank lines up to the @Test. Better, match the test method name convention (for example SEC_HTTP_001_AC2) as CrossAdapterTest names do.

findings.title: The narrowed JS require( heuristic (deferred W3 review item) still has edge misclassifications
findings.description: Reviewed as the W3 report asked. `(.*[^.\w])?require\(` correctly exempts `auth.require(`, and the three new controls (563-566) pin that. Remaining edges: a Java method reference or a qualified static call written `Guards::require(` or `auth .require(` (space before the dot) is still flagged as JavaScript, and JS member calls such as `jwt.require(` are no longer caught. No current page hits either case. Low impact, recorded as still present.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally add `:` and whitespace before `.` to the exemption and add a control for `x::require(`. Otherwise accept it as is.

findings.title: In-memory TestApps started by send() are never shut down (deferred "started TestApps are not shut down")
findings.description: inMemory() starts a new TestApp, with a cached daemon worker pool in InMemoryHttpAdapter, for each setting and peer: six per run of SEC_SVL_001_AC1_AC2_AC3_AC4. None is shut down, so threads and app state are left until JVM exit. The same pattern is in AuthUsersGsonTest (t.send). The threads are daemon and idle out after 60 s, so the impact is small.
findings.suggested_fix: Call t.app().shutdown(...) in a finally block (or add a TestApp.close()), and collect the bodies first.

findings.title: The AC-5 test checks no response values under the hop setting
findings.description: For "hops=1" the body check is skipped entirely, including socketAddress() (the first token), which must still equal the captured getRemoteAddr() 198.51.100.20 under every setting. SEC-SVL-001 AC-5 asks that the exchange values equal the captured values for every setting and header combination. Under hops the test verifies only the call recording.
findings.suggested_fix: Under hops, assert that each body starts with "198.51.100.20 " (socketAddress), and keep the full check for the other settings.
